findings.title: Stored mail cursor is read at fixed version=1 with no expiry or consumption
findings.issue: fetch_page persists and re-reads an opaque continuation record (conversation/cursor_xxx) via get(...,version=1) and only compares payload equality, so the same ref stays valid indefinitely and can be replayed across requests for the same owner/scope/connection. This is read-only pagination, not one-use write confirmation, and each use still requires a fresh grant and reservation, so it is not a fail-open authorization bypass.
findings.fix: Add an explicit expiry timestamp or consume-on-read version fence for stored cursors, and validate the retrieved object's actual version explicitly rather than passing version=1 as a filter. Keep the existing per-call owner/scope/connection/authorization checks as the primary guard.

not_verified: src/prm/capabilities.py and src/prm/runtime/connections.py were not supplied in this packet; authorize_and_reserve, execute_reserved/execute_prepared, revoke semantics and the OAuth credential/refresh path were reviewed only through their call sites in the provided sources.

src/prm/mail_connector.py, src/prm/schedule_connectors.py and src/prm/briefs.py were not supplied; MailScopeSelection/MailFetchRequest field validation and require_mail_read_access semantics are inferred from usage only.
The GraphTransport origin, vault.get secret_ref binding and pa_connections DDL are outside the packet; only the row-level status/account_ref/expiry FOR UPDATE guard at graph.py:80-104 was verified.

Full Postgres immutability of pa_runtime.object_versions (no UPDATE/DELETE grants to pa_test_app) is confirmed at the grant level, but actual enforcement under concurrent writers was not executed here.
The four executable synthetic malformed cases were traced statically (tests/test_pai_graph_mail.py:44-48 and :51-64 against graph.py:_mail_metadata and read_message) but not run in this review.
findings.summary: Focused recheck of the remaining #51 P1 is resolved: read_message now routes both provider date and nested from parsing through _mail_metadata (graph.py:254) and validates body/contentType types (258-261), so the four malformed shapes ('receivedDateTime' invalid/naive, from None or []) raise typed StorageError rather than raw ValueError/AttributeError; the naive-datetime case is explicitly rejected at graph.py:51 and is covered by the parametrized test. Fail-closed behavior holds on the reviewed paths: _guarded_http converts all non-HTTP exceptions to StorageError 'transport outcome unknown' without retry, read grants cannot perform writes (graph.py:70-71), and mail cursors are strictly bound to owner/scope/connection with a fresh authorization each call. Supplied Postgres DDL and grants confirm immutable version rows (SELECT/INSERT only) and that version=1 is a recorded-version selector, not a CAS, which matches the stated semantics. No P0/P1 in the reviewed packet, so verdict is SHIP_OK; scope limits (unreviewed capabilities/connections/mail_connector modules) are recorded separately and do not change the focused decision.
